# Emissions Tracking Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Emissions Tracking Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 9 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the build Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded emissions files, the proposed platform, system and registry sources and the channel; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the verified emissions data platform, the environmental management system and the carbon registry connector; the workshop needs no connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare analyst, compliance, sustainability and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer. | Customer or partner |
| Factor and boundary ownership | Name the owner of approved emissions factors, organizational boundaries and units before any total is used. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sustainability program owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Inventory reconciliation effort and screening-to-verification gaps by facility. Agree how slow and error-prone reconciliation is today before attributing any change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Facility | Reporting period | Scopes reconciled | Reconciliation effort | Factor or boundary issues | Items sent for verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree data sources, factor and boundary controls, governance, support, telemetry and success measures.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sustainability program owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Sustainability program owner | Approve scope, data sources, factor and boundary controls and success measures; never treat synthetic figures as verified results. |
| Qualified sustainability and regulatory reviewers | Own attestations, compliance determinations, disclosures and external actions; review reduction scenarios with engineering, finance and executives. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, environment access, authenticated audience and data policies before emissions data is connected. |
| Emissions data connection owners | Approve least-privilege emissions platform, environmental system and registry connections and their identities; own access failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check EMISSION_TRACKING-01 through EMISSION_TRACKING-04 and the boundary tests on full responses; reject reshoot-required captures. |
| Operations owner | Own session and credit monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route claims and transactions to qualified reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed with named owners.
- [ ] The program owner records how inventory, thresholds, targets and offsets are reconciled today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/emission-tracking/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve file, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and maker access are recorded, and the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available there.
- [ ] Authenticated reviewer access and only the necessary emissions-data scopes are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/emission-tracking/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/emission-tracking/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/emission-tracking/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/emission-tracking/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Emissions Tracking Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: emission-tracking-rules-and-controls.md
7. Add knowledge: emission-tracking-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_carbon-offset-analysis
9. Add skill: aibast_compliance-status
10. Add skill: aibast_emissions-dashboard
11. Add skill: aibast_reduction-plan
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass EMISSION_TRACKING-01: Emissions Data Analyst
15. Pass EMISSION_TRACKING-02: Environmental Compliance Manager
16. Pass EMISSION_TRACKING-03: Decarbonization Program Lead
17. Pass EMISSION_TRACKING-04: Sustainability Lead
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: EMISSION_TRACKING-01, EMISSION_TRACKING-02, EMISSION_TRACKING-03, EMISSION_TRACKING-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The chosen lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is used, the smoke test calls `EmissionTrackingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in a separate fresh conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on the full final response; an annotated screenshot does not replace the machine gate.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before emissions or registry data is reachable. Request only read scopes for the four review skills. Restrict the reviewer audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Verified emissions data platform

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Emissions data connection owners

1. **Bind Verified emissions data platform — read:** Bind an approved read-only connector, API or MCP tool.

2. **Identity for Verified emissions data platform:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Verified emissions data platform:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Verified emissions data platform:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Verify and disclose nothing; the inventory is unverified synthetic evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so; never substitute another record.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Environmental management system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Emissions data connection owners

1. **Bind Environmental management system — read:** Bind read-only actions first; keep any workflow write separate and audited.

2. **Identity for Environmental management system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Environmental management system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Environmental management system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the identifier is absent; never substitute another facility. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so; never substitute another record.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Approved emissions-factor and boundary controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Emissions data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved emissions-factor and boundary controls — read:** Add owner-approved factor and boundary knowledge and record its content owner.

2. **Identity for Approved emissions-factor and boundary controls:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved emissions-factor and boundary controls:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved emissions-factor and boundary controls:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not browse for replacement facts; use only the packaged evidence. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the missing evidence; never claim a filing, purchase or claim succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved carbon registry connector

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Emissions data connection owners

1. **Bind Approved carbon registry connector — read:** Bind authenticated read-only registry lookups; keep transactions outside the agent.

2. **Identity for Approved carbon registry connector:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved carbon registry connector:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved carbon registry connector:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Buy and retire nothing; the shortlist is due diligence only and makes no offset claim. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the missing evidence; never claim a filing, purchase or claim succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams for qualified review

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Emissions data connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams for qualified review — write:** Route drafts to an approved review workflow; nothing is filed or disclosed (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams for qualified review:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams for qualified review:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams for qualified review:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Declare no legal compliance; give the screening result and route to qualified regulatory reviewers. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Decline; name the qualified reviewer and the approved production connection needed next.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Emissions data connection owners

Replace synthetic records with least-privilege read connectors first; keep any write tool separate and audited.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Read connectors come first; any write tool is separate, confirmed by an authorized role, validated against current state and audit-logged.
- [ ] Approved sources preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no filing, purchase or claim is reported without tool evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test reviewer and unshared identities in an approved test deployment; a maker's access does not prove user access.

### Step 4-3. Validate factors

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Qualified sustainability and regulatory reviewers

Validate factors, boundaries, units and gas coverage in totals before evaluating customer data.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The program owner sets acceptance measures on customer data after factors and boundaries are validated; synthetic figures are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked emissions corpus | All four cases, EMISSION_TRACKING-01 through EMISSION_TRACKING-04, satisfy every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Claim and transaction boundary | Any verified-claim statement, legal compliance declaration, credit purchase or retirement, disclosure or filing is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoints | Reusable captures show a positive anchor; reshoot-required captures are withheld. |
| Release state | The validated manual and pilot agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sustainability program owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Sustainability program owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved reviewer audience and channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, absent-identifier answers, connection errors and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, authentication errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
